newsitem.title: USA: Merck rebounds as bargain-hunters move in.
newsitem.headline: Merck rebounds as bargain-hunters move in.

text.p: Shares of Merck & Co Inc rebounded in early trading Thursday as bargain-hunters moved in following the stock's sharp decline yesterday.
The shares rose 1-7/8 to 83-3/8 in heavy trading on the New York Stock Exchange. More than 1.8 million shares had changed hands by mid-morning.
The stock fell 3-3/4 to 81-1/2 Wednesday on speculation that Warner-Lambert Co's new cholesterol-cutting drug Lipitor could cut into sales of Merck's popular drugs Zocor and Mevacor.
Mariola Haggar, who covers Merck for Deutsche Morgan Grenfell, said in a research note that Merck's stock tumble was an overreaction
She said the cholesterol-reducing drug market is big enough and is growing rapidly at 20 and 25 percent.

She said Merck will soon publish data showing that Zocor lowers triglycerides almost as much as Lipitor. Currently, lowering triglycerides is a feature perceived as unique to Lipitor, she said in the report.
Gruntal & Co analyst Adam Greene, in a research note, reiterated his strong buy recommendation on Merck and said the price weakness presented a good buying opportunity.

He said he expects Merck to post first quarter earnings per share growth of 18 to 19 percent and said "management is still comfortable with the EPS (earnings per share) range of $3.70 to $3.85" for all of 1997. He said Merck is to report first quarter results around April 16.
Haggar is maintaining her 1997 profit estimate at $3.80 a share. She expects Merck to post first quarter earnings per share of $0.83, compared to $0.70 a year ago.
